overall_risk_rationale: Guest ratings are generally positive (avg rating increased slightly to 7.83) and revenue metrics improved, but repeated negative comments about spa/facilities, front-desk service, cleanliness and supplies create a moderate reputational and operational risk if not addressed promptly.
executive_summary: Recent reviews show strengths in location, ocean views, breakfast quality and many positive staff interactions, but recurring operational issues require attention: (1) front-desk service and check-in handling, (2) wellness/spa and top-floor facilities out of service, (3) cleanliness concerns, (4) guest supplies and late-night food availability, and (5) inconsistent guest communication about operating hours/closures. Addressing these with immediate operational fixes, targeted maintenance, staff training and clearer guest communication should protect reputation and guest repeat business.

priorities.problem: Multiple reviews cite reception staff 'attitude problems', arrogance and poor handling of late/ delayed check-ins (room not ready, no apology, no proactive communication). This directly affects guest experience and perceived service quality.
priorities.recommended_action: Run immediate refresher training for front-desk staff on service standards, empathy and communication. Implement a standard operating procedure (SOP) for delayed room readiness including proactive guest notification, apology script, and offered compensation (drink/discount/early breakfast). Institute a simple front-desk feedback metric (post-check-in micro-survey) and weekly coaching based on responses.
priorities.rationale: A single negative interaction at check-in is highly salient and several reviews describe the same problem; fixing behavior and communication is low-cost and high-impact on guest satisfaction.
supporting_evidence: 2024-09-12 review: 'Reception staff have an attitude problem... Our room wasn't ready for check in on time... they didn't even apologise and just left us sitting about... arrogant and disinterested and spoilt our stay.'

priorities.problem: Multiple guests report jacuzzi/spa and top-floor facilities being out of service or closed early; this undermines expectations for a 4-star property and for guests who specifically booked for wellness facilities.
priorities.recommended_action: Conduct an immediate technical inspection of the wellness area and top-floor facilities to diagnose faults and establish a repair timeline. If immediate repair is not possible, close affected areas formally with clear signage, update OTAs/website and pre-arrival communications, and offer affected guests compensation (waiver, discount, or alternate amenity). Review maintenance scheduling and spare-parts stock to reduce recurrence. If recurring breakdowns are frequent, initiate a capital assessment for replacement.
priorities.rationale: Repeated mentions across reviews indicate this is not a one-off issue. Proactive repair + clear communications restore trust and limit negative reviews/bookings from disappointed guests.
supporting_evidence: 2024-09-19 review: 'Facilities on the top floor were not working.'
2024-09-16 review: 'We chose the hotel because of the jacuzzis, but they closed the wellness area very soon, so there was no chance to use it.'

priorities.problem: At least one review scores the stay low specifically because of cleanliness issues ('Limpeza'), indicating a housekeeping lapse that can strongly reduce guest satisfaction.
priorities.recommended_action: Perform an immediate housekeeping audit (spot checks) of recently departed rooms and common areas. Retrain housekeeping staff on checklist standards, introduce a short per-room checklist signed at inspection, increase supervisor inspections for a period, and respond to the negative review publicly explaining corrective actions taken.
priorities.rationale: Cleanliness is a baseline expectation; addressing housekeeping lapses improves guest comfort and prevents negative word-of-mouth.

priorities.problem: Guests reported minimal toiletries (no shampoo, tiny dispenser output) and lack of food options for very late arrivals ('arrived at half past midnight and there was nothing to eat'). These reduce perceived value and convenience.
priorities.recommended_action: Review and standardize in-room toiletry provisioning (add shampoo, check dispenser flow rates and refill schedule). Establish a late-arrival offering (small grab-and-go snacks or a simple refrigerated shelf, or partner with a nearby vendor/room-service on-call). Ensure front desk informs late arrivals about available options.
priorities.rationale: These are relatively low-cost fixes that improve guest experience and perceived value, especially for guests who arrive late or expect basic amenities.
supporting_evidence: 2024-09-16 review: 'They provided very few toiletries, only a hotel soap and a shower gel... There was no shampoo, and the shower gel dispenser dispensed microscopic amounts.'
2024-09-15 review: 'We arrived at half past midnight and there was nothing to eat anywhere.'

priorities.area: Guest communication & expectations about operating hours/closures
priorities.problem: Guests expected to use wellness facilities but encountered unexpected closures or early closing times; lack of proactive communication amplified disappointment.
priorities.recommended_action: Update all booking channels (hotel website, OTAs) with current wellness hours and any temporary closures. Add a pre-arrival email and front-desk script to inform guests about operating hours and alternative options. Train reservations staff to mention operating hours during booking for guests who request spa/wellness.
priorities.rationale: Clear, proactive communication reduces expectation gaps and avoids negative reviews from preventable disappointments.
supporting_evidence: 2024-09-16 review: 'We chose the hotel because of the jacuzzis, but they closed the wellness area very soon...'
2024-09-19 review: 'Facilities on the top floor were not working.'

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Multiple reviews praise location and very nice views; location is a clear differentiator and attraction for guests.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Preserve room types/views allocation, promote views in marketing, ensure public spaces / breakfast area continue to capitalize on scenery.

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Several guests describe the breakfast as tasty and the coffee positively; breakfast is a recurring positive touchpoint.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Keep breakfast standards and offerings, maintain consistency in service and food quality.

strengths_to_preserve.area: Friendly staff interactions (where present) and value for money
strengths_to_preserve.reason: Some reviews explicitly praise staff kindness, parking availability and value for money.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Recognize and reward staff who receive positive comments; replicate behaviors through training and staff briefings.

monitoring_indicators.reason: Broad measure of guest satisfaction trends.

monitoring_indicators.indicator: Number of reviews mentioning 'spa' / 'jacuzzi' downtime or 'facilities not working' (monthly)
monitoring_indicators.reason: Tracks recurrence and guest impact of wellness-area problems.

monitoring_indicators.indicator: Number of front-desk complaints / negative check-in comments (monthly) and post-check-in micro-survey score
monitoring_indicators.reason: Measures improvement in check-in service and staff attitude.

monitoring_indicators.indicator: Housekeeping audit pass rate (percent of inspected rooms meeting standards)
Incidents of toiletry stockouts or dispenser refill intervals (weekly)
monitoring_indicators.reason: Monitors supply issues that lead to guest complaints.

monitoring_indicators.indicator: Number of late-arrival food requests unmet / guest complaints about food availability at night
monitoring_indicators.reason: Monitors effectiveness of late-night food offering.

limitations: Analysis uses only the supplied 20 most-recent reviews (out of 36 available in the window); frequency estimates of issues may be imprecise.
Customer comments are qualitative and may reflect individual experiences; they do not establish causation for financial performance changes.
Some problems (e.g., how often wellness facilities break down) require operational data/maintenance logs for full root-cause diagnosis.
No breakdown provided of which room types or arrival channels most affected by the issues; targeted interventions may need additional segmentation data.
